root_cause_label: False Premise on Account Number Completeness with Self-Referential Validation
one_sentence_failure_summary: The agent assumed that the account numbers visible in company-name-matched rows were the complete set, wrote a filtering script with exact account-number matching that silently omits typo variants (e.g., BUS-30g01), then validated the output against the same flawed criteria, producing a false 'zero missing rows' result.
t_err_evidence: In step 10 the agent writes process.py using exact account-number matching (row['Account Number'] in account_numbers) without any normalization or fuzzy handling; it collected only BUS-30001, BUS-30999, BUS-35001 from the name-matched rows, treating that set as exhaustive despite the task's explicit mention of typos in account numbers.
t_commit_evidence: Step 11 executes process.py which writes output.json with 8 rows. The agent never revises the filtering logic after this point; all subsequent steps perform verification or cosmetic checks against the already-written output, locking in the incomplete result.
trigger_explanation: The agent observed three account numbers (BUS-30001, BUS-30999, BUS-35001) from grep results in step 5 and implicitly treated them as the complete canonical set. It never considered that the same logical account could appear with a typoed number (BUS-30g01) in other rows, even though the task specification explicitly warns of typos. This unverified assumption about set completeness was embedded directly into the filtering script.
